headline: Loss narrows sharply as refinancing extends debt runway
summary_short: MPT's Q2 2026 net loss narrowed to $2.6M (-$0.01/share) from $98.4M (-$0.16/share) a year ago as revenue rose 7.9% to $259.3M and Normalized FFO climbed 13.4% to $92.2M ($0.15/share).
summary_long: Net loss narrowed to $2.6M ($0.01/share) from $98.4M a year ago, mainly because a $124.4M prior-year non-cash fair-value charge shrank to $1.9M this quarter. Revenue rose 7.9% to $259.3M as transition tenants continued ramping rent payments. Normalized FFO grew 13.4% to $92.2M ($0.15/share); Nareit FFO swung to $78.1M from a $40.2M loss. Interest expense rose 4.3% to $135.3M. Cash fell 6.7% q/q to $396.6M and equity edged down 1.0% q/q, while debt was roughly flat at $9,705.0M. Subsequent to quarter-end, MPT closed a $2.4B note refinancing extending maturities and expects ~$172M from a pending asset sale in Q3. Dividend raised to $0.09/share.

drivers.explanation: CEO cited strong performance across the global operator portfolio and transition tenants ramping rent payments as expected, alongside continued balance-sheet actions (refinancing, asset sales).
Loss narrowed mainly because 'Other (including fair value adjustments on securities)' fell to a $1.9M expense from $124.4M a year ago, per the income statement.
Rent billed rose to $203.4M from $177.9M y/y; the release attributes portfolio strength to transition tenants ramping rent payments as expected, without a dollar-by-dollar breakdown.
EPS improved in step with the narrower net loss; weighted average diluted shares were little changed at 597.96M.
NFFO growth mirrors the net loss narrowing and revenue growth flowing through the Nareit-to-normalized reconciliation; no single driver is called out separately in the release.
Per-share NFFO rose in step with aggregate NFFO growth; diluted share count was little changed y/y.
FFO swung positive as the net loss narrowed and the depreciation/amortization add-back rose slightly to $86.0M from $81.3M, per the reconciliation table.
Not explained in the release; the increase is consistent with a larger average debt balance carried ahead of the August 10 refinancing.
Not broken out as a single driver; likely reflects the dividend payment, the quarter's $50M HSA working-capital advance, and other investing/financing outflows.
Balance was little-changed during the quarter itself; the $2.4B refinancing that reshapes maturities closed August 10, after quarter-end.
Accumulated other comprehensive income fell roughly $33M on currency translation, and dividends declared exceeded net income, both pulling equity down q/q.
Board declared $0.09/share for the quarter, up from $0.08 a year ago and unchanged from Q1 2026.
